commands:
set -uo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Regression suite: the repository's own pre-existing shared-utils tests.
#    They are NOT modified by tests.patch and they link the same runtime
#    sources the task changes, so they catch collateral damage to ordinary
#    allocation. Built against the system gtest that the image already ships,
#    so the airgapped verifier needs no downloads.
#    bh_queue_test_suite.bh_queue_get_message_count is excluded: at base it
#    posts one message pointer into the queue 20 times, so the queue frees the
#    same allocation repeatedly. That double free is a defect in the test, and
#    the upstream PR rewrote the test for exactly this reason.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat > /tmp/gtest_inject.cmake <<'CMK'
find_package(GTest REQUIRED)
if(NOT TARGET gtest_main)
  add_library(gtest_main INTERFACE)
  target_link_libraries(gtest_main INTERFACE GTest::gtest_main GTest::gtest)
endif()
include(GoogleTest)
CMK
SU_BUILD=/tmp/shared-utils-build
rm -rf "$SU_BUILD"
# Build output goes to a file, never to the graded stream.
cmake -S tests/unit/shared-utils -B "$SU_BUILD" -DWAMR_BUILD_PLATFORM=linux -DLLVM_DIR=IGNORE \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_PROJECT_INCLUDE=/tmp/gtest_inject.cmake > /tmp/su_configure.log 2>&1 \
  || echo "regression suite: cmake configure failed, see /tmp/su_configure.log"
cmake --build "$SU_BUILD" -j"$(nproc)" > /tmp/su_build.log 2>&1 \
  || echo "regression suite: build failed, see /tmp/su_build.log"
if [ -x "$SU_BUILD/shared_utils_test" ]; then
  "$SU_BUILD/shared_utils_test" --gtest_filter=-bh_queue_test_suite.bh_queue_get_message_count
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Feature suite: the graded aligned-allocation tests.
#    Only mem-alloc-test is run. The CMakeLists also defines mem-alloc-gc-test,
#    but it registers the same test names, and duplicate names collapse in the
#    grader, so running both would let a result from one binary mask the other.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat > /tmp/mem_alloc_inject.cmake <<'CMK'
find_path(CMOCKA_INCLUDE_DIR cmocka.h)
find_library(CMOCKA_LIB NAMES cmocka)
if(NOT CMOCKA_INCLUDE_DIR OR NOT CMOCKA_LIB)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "cmocka not found")
endif()
if(NOT TARGET cmocka::cmocka)
  add_library(cmocka::cmocka UNKNOWN IMPORTED)
  set_target_properties(cmocka::cmocka PROPERTIES IMPORTED_LOCATION "${CMOCKA_LIB}" INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${CMOCKA_INCLUDE_DIR}")
endif()
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS} -include stdarg.h -include stddef.h -include setjmp.h")
CMK
BUILD=/tmp/mem-alloc-build
rm -rf "$BUILD"
# --coverage instruments the graded suite so the harness can prove afterwards
# that the assertions really executed, rather than trusting printed markers.
cmake -S tests/unit/mem-alloc -B "$BUILD" -DWAMR_BUILD_PLATFORM=linux -DLLVM_DIR=IGNORE \
      -DCMAKE_PROJECT_test-mem-alloc_INCLUDE=/tmp/mem_alloc_inject.cmake \
      -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="--coverage" -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="--coverage" > /tmp/ma_configure.log 2>&1 \
  || echo "feature suite: cmake configure failed, see /tmp/ma_configure.log"
cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)" > /tmp/ma_build.log 2>&1 \
  || echo "feature suite: build failed, see /tmp/ma_build.log"
if [ -x "$BUILD/mem-alloc-test" ]; then
  CMOCKA_MESSAGE_OUTPUT=STDOUT "$BUILD/mem-alloc-test"
fi
